A wild coyote named Wendy is going viral in Los Angeles because of a huge growth on her face.

She has been living like this for over a year, and people in the neighborhood know her by name and have seen her walking near homes and standing at people's doors.

Wildlife Care of Southern California has been trying to catch her for weeks so they can examine her, X-ray the growth, and finally give her medical treatment.

The rescue organization also posted on Facebook asking people to donate to help cover the rescue equipment and Wendy’s upcoming vet bills.

Flock cameras are automated license plate reader cameras used across the United States to identify and track vehicles. They can capture license plates and vehicle details, creating records of when and where a vehicle was seen.

The controversy is about what can happen when thousands of cameras, police databases and AI-powered tools are connected. Critics fear that this technology could make it possible to reconstruct people’s movements and create a massive surveillance network.

That’s why people are pushing back. Communities have protested against Flock cameras, demanded their removal, and in some cases cameras have even been vandalized or taken down.
